references.observation: The site plan describes the enlarged pavilion adjacent to First Palace, with three terraces framing the raised open stage and a passage beneath the main seating.
The visitor photo shows the broad ramp entering off-center, separated rear seat banks, low stepped fascia, projecting timber caps and clay-colored reliefs on the wings.
Behind the foreground sculpture, a low straight roof, a raised stage and a terracotta wing panel share the features of the wide visitor photo.
Figure 31 identifies an artistically decorated podium used for the annual festival. The September 2023 pavilion photo supplies a wide exterior view of the ramp, seating and reliefs.

The offset access ramp, the dark gap beneath the right seating, three banks, continuous low eaves and little pointed eave caps match the earlier photographs. A terracotta finish covers the stage risers, terrace faces and square posts. The right relief rises toward the outer post. The image contains no geographic coordinates.

placementTrial.limitations: A fit of the stage corner, relief panel, post and low canopy in the geotagged 2022 portrait supports a south to southwest approach. The draft faces approximately 194 degrees true. The point fit is moved 4 m north, within the recorded 4.7 m camera uncertainty, to leave about 6 m between the fitted footprints. Several equally plausible free-scale fits overlap First Palace. Pavilion coordinates, footprint and heading remain approximate.

forecourtGradeTrial.basis: The 2022 portrait and the wide pavilion photo show a relatively even space beyond the ramp toe. The profile fits that immediate forecourt and tapers up toward the retained First Palace grade.
forecourtGradeTrial.limitation: The wider hillside transition is a terrain-fit estimate. The photographed floor, the First Palace model and the original Terrarium field constrain the reconstruction.
